assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 500,000 events/s peak; 98% are click/impression writes, ~1.9% advertiser dashboard reads, 0.1% a replay/reconciliation pass over the archive.

assumptions.subject: batching
assumptions.statement: Every downstream fan-out is BATCHED, and batching is modelled as a visit_prob below 1.0: the archive writer flushes one object per 50 events (0.02), the aggregator pipelines one Redis update per 20 events (0.05), and the rollup flush writes one row per 1,000 events (0.001). Those three numbers are the whole reason a 500k/s firehose lands on one PostgreSQL primary.

assumptions.subject: agg
assumptions.statement: The aggregator is windowed in-memory counting at ~12k events/s per instance. Exactly-once semantics, watermarking and late-event handling are NOT modelled — the engine is an open queueing network with no notion of event time.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: Counts drive advertiser billing, so the rollup store is the money-of-record. This design is flagged high-stakes:payments and needs expert review before production; the engine sizes it, it does not certify it.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Compute only. Kafka storage, object-store GB and cross-AZ transfer are not priced; at 500k events/s cross-AZ traffic is a material line this model omits.

_library.summary: High-volume click ingest into a log, streaming windowed aggregation into hot counters, and batched rollups into a billable aggregate store.
